result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend the same thing: explicit modes, with Select as the default, Paint armed on purpose, and Record as a separate action with a specific overwrite confirmation and an always-visible undo. A edges ahead because it states the cost of modes directly (switching takes time, and operators forget which mode they're in) and says how its design handles that. It also adds useful show-time details: the mode label sits where the operator is looking, the indicator doesn't rely on color alone, and the selection count stays visible. B's show-lock and hold-to-paint fallback fit a live show well, but its 'revert on lift' rule would force the operator to re-arm Paint after every stroke. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend the same variant: explicit Select and Paint modes, with Record as a separate deliberate action. Both also explain the specific costs of the gesture design. B goes further on show-time safety: its indicator uses a label and not just color, it keeps the selection visible with a count, and its Record confirmation names the cue it will overwrite. It also keeps undo-first painting fast and offers a visible shortcut so switching modes stays quick. A is strong but less detailed, and its 'revert to Select on a lift' rule is a bit muddled.
